observations:
Torah #176 is a very short teaching (3 paragraphs) with a tightly unified single-thread argument. After reviewing all three dataset edges (all eitza) and the full source text, no cluster of 3 or more bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain was identified that would qualify as a new package beyond what the gap analysis already proposes.

The only bechina relationship detected in the source text is the single identity pair: רוח שטות ↔ אויר (see torah_176_additions.json). Two nodes do not meet the 3+ threshold for a new package proposal.

All other conceptual actors in this teaching — הצדיק האמת, אהבת נפש / היתקשרות, נכלל לבו בלב הצדיק, לב הצדיק חלל, מקום פנוי, לב נשבר — are connected through eitza (causal/directional) relationships, not bechina (shared-nature) relationships. They form a causal chain: [connect to Tzaddik with love] → [heart included in Tzaddik's hollow heart] → [ruach shtut escapes with urgency] → [broken heart]. This is a single eitza thread, not a bechina cluster.

The רוח שטות ↔ אויר pair is the only bechina equivalence and it is assigned to Package 1 (רוח שטות ואויר) in torah_176_packages.json, which is itself derived from the gap analysis rather than from dataset edges. There is no independent third domain visible in either the dataset or the source text that would qualify for a new package.

Conclusion: No new packages are proposed for Torah #176.
